title: Waypoint Hublet Portal: mesh-based console navigation prototype and IA review
creator: Maya Patel
description:
Problem: As teams scale across orgs and projects, the current vertical rail and flat workspace switcher cause cognitive load when locating routes for dashboards, rollouts, and cost views. Existing patterns either hide context (deep links) or require many clicks to switch roles and compare cost lenses.

Proposal: Introduce a mesh-based 'Waypoint Hublet' navigation pattern — compact hublets that surface contextual entry points (Dashboards, Rollouts, Cost Lenses, Models, Deployments) grouped by intent and user role. Each hublet is a small portal that preserves session anchors (last-opened view, pinned cost lens) and exposes micro-actions (open in new tab, pin to workspace, quick compare). Hublets can expand into transient overlays for fast task flows without full route changes.

Design goals: Reduce route-switch time, surface cost-relevant controls earlier, maintain keyboard-first accessibility, provide clear affordances for canary/A-B rollout states, and allow role-aware filtering. Preserve backwards compatibility for power users who prefer the classic left rail.

Constraints and trade-offs: Mesh hublets require lightweight client-side routing and prefetching of small view fragments. This increases initial bundle complexity and client memory for active hublets. We prioritized modest prefetch heuristics (recently-used hublets and top N by role) to limit overhead. Fallbacks to server-side routes retained for low-memory environments (private deployments).
acceptance_criteria: Prototype available in Figma and interactive FigJam with annotated flows
Design review signoff from PM (Kieran Blake) and Eng lead (Rina Gupta)
Usability test (6 participants) shows median task completion time <= 40% of baseline for switching between Dashboards and Cost Lenses
Keyboard navigation works end-to-end and meets A11y contrast ratios
Engineering has documented required client-side routing hooks and prefetch heuristics
Rollout experiment plan with success metrics and rollback criteria created
comments: 2026-02-22 Maya Patel: Initial low-fi sketches posted to FigJam. Focused on grouping by "intent" (inspect, compare, act) rather than by resource type.
2026-02-27 Ethan Ruiz: Iterated on micro-actions (pin/compare/open). Added compact affordance for cost-lens toggle to hublet header.
2026-03-03 Kieran Blake (PM): Loved intent grouping; asked for explicit fallbacks for customers on private deploys and a plan for telemetry to measure detours after hublet opens.

2026-03-05 Rina Gupta (Eng): Raised concerns about prefetch budget on low-memory hosts. Agreed to a configurable heuristic (recent N + role-priority) and to gate aggressive prefetching behind a feature flag for Dedicated/Hosted.

2026-03-08 Usability session summary: 6 participants (3 platform engineers, 2 product managers, 1 support rep). Observed confusion when multiple hublets expanded; resolved with clearer close affordances and escape-to-previous-route behavior. Median task time improved from 28s to 12s for switching cost lenses.
2026-03-10 Design critique: Accessibility team requested focus ring improvements and ARIA labels for hublet micro-actions. Added keyboard grouping and announced status changes for canary rollouts.
2026-03-12 Ethan Ruiz: Built an interactive HTML prototype for eng to test routing hooks. Linked in attachments. Noted issues with scroll restoration; eng tracking as ENG-4812.
2026-03-14 Maya Patel: Submitted for design review. Requested reviewers to sign off on trade-offs (prefetch budget, accessibility edge cases) and on the rollout experiment plan.
review_notes: PM feedback: Add metrics hooks for 'detour' and 'hublet abandonment' to measure UX regressions.
Eng feedback: Provide clear API for route anchors and a maximum prefetch budget that can be tuned per deployment tier.
Design ops: Recommend a phased rollout: opt-in beta -> 10% canary -> 50% -> full, with rollback criteria based on error rates and task completion time.
Accessibility: Ensure live region announcements for hublet open/close and accessible descriptions for micro-actions.
